chapter: Desvigne, Chicago offers and Peter Hone's band
title: Peter Hone's society-circuit jobs and singer Harry Wells during the Depression
summary: Hone's band holds country club and fraternity work and uses singer Harry Wells, in the Depression years around 1930-33.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Yeah, I didn't get that. Alfred William on drum. drums. So Peter Hone had nice work like the field work like it is now playing like at the New Orleans Country Club. He had that tied up. Anything that was out there, he was a house band because they had a man named Mr. Crawford Ellis. That's the man that's got interest in Boat Young, a little bit around the South American and the Pan American insurance. And he liked the Peter Hone band. And then we had work like at the metric club and then we had work like out the Ottoman Park and we used to play for those like the kids, what you call them, we call them the frat house with plenty of houses. And then Peter Hone had a nice connection with like I know of the autocrat clubs. And at the time they had something they would hire his band and they liked it, what he called his second band, which is really his, because he had put the first band down, you see, because it was a regular ten piece band. Then he had a fellow named Harry Wells sing. Harry Wells was like a fellow like I'd call Earl Williams today. He could sing London songs fast, he could sing pop tunes and he could sing blues and everything and he could pick up on the song right away, you see, because we could come there with music and we'd play once or twice and he had it. That was during the Depression. Oh, that's during the Depression. So we, uh, that was about, I can say about the year, about the year of 30, 32 or 33. I was living on Prairie in La Hampa. Yeah, yeah. So Gene, he stayed with Sidney and Sidney, Sidney had the job on the boat then I believe, because Sidney had the job on the boat and I first left there. I stood, that was 1930 I remember. We had played that, because that was the first time we had played, the boat had been up to St. Paul in many years and that was, that was a terrific day. But he had gotten background back by 33 or 34. Well anyhow, I stayed with you on band.
